title: Redwood + Silverpine Bank: Security / BCDR / Incident Response Review
summary: Review of Redwood incident response, BCDR (RTO/RPO), SLA uptime guarantees, and escalation matrix. Customer raised questions on SOC 2 evidence, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log retention, and multi-region failover testing. Agreed next steps: share incident runbook, proposed SLA addendum, run a DR tabletop with Silverpine ops team, and schedule a dedicated civil engineering pilot for RPO/RTO benchmarks.
topics: BCDR: RTO/RPO targets and testing cadence
RBAC / SSO integration and audit logging
transcript:
00:00 Maya Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're running about an hour, we'll cover IR, BCDR, and SLA escalation. I think Ravi is going to walk through the playbook and then we'll open up for Qs.
00:12 Jon Keller: Sounds good. We're hoping to get specifics on RTO/RPO and how Redwood handles cross-region failover for private deployments. Also want to validate SOC 2 artifacts.
00:23 Ravi Patel: Great — quick agenda, intro to incident response, detection and classification, containment and mitigation, communication and post-mortem. Then BCDR specifics — backup frequency, RPOs, recovery drills, and the SLA side.
00:38 Maya Ortiz: Jon, can you remind us of Silverpine's requirements? I remember RTOs for critical payments flows are tight, like under 15 minutes for failover?
00:45 Jon Keller: Yes, for our payments API we need RTO < 15, RPO near-zero for transactional logs; for analytics workloads RTOs can be hours. Also we need clear escalation to our SOC and CISO mailbox.
00:58 Aisha Rahman: And from ops side, we want to ensure the private deployable stack can be tested in our VPC without leaking keys or logs.
01:07 Ravi Patel: Understood. High level: for hosted we have automated multi-region routing and warm standby variants; for Private deployments we offer an optional active/standby architecture. RTOs depend on whether KV caches are warm — for cold start it's longer. We typically guarantee RTOs in Dedicated contracts; for Private we do runbooks and can build an SLA addendum.
01:30 Priya Desai: When you say "KV cache warm", can you clarify — are you keeping persistent KV across failover? Because we rely on session/continuation tokens.
01:38 Ravi Patel: Good callout. The runtime uses a combination of persistent storage for model artifacts and ephemeral KV caches for in-flight session cache. For strict RPOs we recommend enabling prefix/KV persistent checkpointing to object storage. That reduces RPO to near-zero for model state, but it does add a small write latency — tradeoff.
01:55 Jon Keller: What about encryption — we need keys in our KMS, not Redwood-managed keys. We have a policy: customer-managed KMS only.
02:02 Maya Ortiz: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM. We keep an audit trail of all key usage. I'll share the KMS integration doc after.
02:12 Liam Chen: Audit logs — retention and tamper evidence? We need 7 years for certain logs for compliance.
02:18 Ravi Patel: Our default audit log retention is 365 days in hosted; for Private deployments you can configure retention and export to your SIEM. For tamper-evidence, we support append-only storage with signed manifests and we can push to your WORM-compatible object store. We'll provide the list of supported sinks.
02:34 Jon Keller: SOC 2 evidence — can you provide the Type II attestation and the last three-year of penetration testing summaries?
02:41 Maya Ortiz: We can share the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; pen test summaries we can share redacted reports. I'll have those links in the follow-up.
02:49 Aisha Rahman: On escalation flow — if something impacts the payments latency we need a direct phone escalation to an on-call SE and an ops lead, and an SRE manager looped in. How does Redwood handle paging?
02:59 Ravi Patel: Our escalation matrix has three tiers. Tier 1 is engineering on-call for the runtime, Tier 2 is SE/PM lead, Tier 3 is executive on-call for enterprise incidents. For Dedicated customers we can add a direct phone bridge and a dedicated Slack/email pager. We also document RACI in the runbook.
03:20 Priya Desai: Do you have runbooks and playbooks templates? We want to align our own SOPs to yours so drills are smoother.
03:27 Ravi Patel: Yes, we have incident playbooks per class: network outage, full-region loss, degraded throughput, data integrity event. I'll send the runbook and a tabletop script.
03:34 Jon Keller: Can we test failover monthly or quarterly? We prefer quarterly drills and one full failover per year.
03:40 Maya Ortiz: Quarterly drills are ok; we'll recommend a staging rehearsal first then a controlled production failover. For Dedicated we can schedule a blue/green cutover.
03:48 Liam Chen: SLA credits — how are uptime measured? 99.9? 99.95? And the measurement window?
03:54 Ravi Patel: Our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly for API availability; Dedicated customers often select 99.95 with an enterprise addendum. We measure at the per-model endpoint level and calculate downtime as error/latency SLO breaches. Credits are pro-rated and detailed in the SLA schedule.
04:12 Jon Keller: We need tighter guarantees for payments. Is 99.95 realistic?
04:16 Maya Ortiz: Yes, with Dedicated reserved capacity, autoscaling and priority routing, 99.95 is realistic — and we include dedicated capacity commitments and a bridge for emergency inflight capacity. We'll surface the SLA addendum for you to review.
04:28 Aisha Rahman: On RTO testing — how do you validate RPO for KV/prefix caching? We need objective metrics.
04:35 Ravi Patel: We'll run a DR experiment where we fail the primary and measure time to successful requests and cache warm-up. We capture tail latency and token throughput, and produce an RTO/RPO report. We recommend doing this in a pre-prod mirror first.
04:50 Jon Keller: Escalation contact list — can you include 24/7 phone numbers?
04:54 Maya Ortiz: Yes, we'll include on-call rotation and contact numbers in the runbook. For enterprise we can do a dedicated phone line and an SSO-protected incident portal.
05:04 Priya Desai: SSO and RBAC — we use SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and want per-tenant RBAC controls.
05:12 Ravi Patel: We support SAML with SCIM, OIDC as well, and fine-grained RBAC. For Private deployments RBAC can integrate with your AD. We'll share the RBAC schema and sample roles.
05:24 Liam Chen: How are access logs structured? We need immutable records tying apiKey or principal to actions; also we need signed audit trails for compliance.
05:33 Ravi Patel: Audit events include principal, action, resource, timestamp, and request hash. We can stream to your SIEM or to a secure S3 bucket with object locking. The logs are signed with a Redwood HSM key if you want tamper-evidence.
05:46 Jon Keller: Anything around data residency? All PII must stay in-region.
05:50 Maya Ortiz: Data residency is configurable; for Private we run entirely within your VPC/region. For hosted, we have region pins and controls; we can sign a DPA with residency clauses.
05:59 Aisha Rahman: One scenario: a crypto compromise where keys were exfiltrated. Walk me through steps.
06:06 Ravi Patel: If keys are suspected exfiltrated, immediate step is taking affected keys out of rotation, rotating CMKs, revoking active sessions, and initiating incident classification. Redwood will convene the incident commander, notify your security contacts, and execute containment playbooks. Post-mortem and forensic evidence will be provided. We also support immediate key rewrap via your KMS.
06:27 Jon Keller: Do you do runbook dry runs with customers?
06:30 Maya Ortiz: Yes, we offer tabletop drills and live failover rehearsals as part of our onboarding package for enterprise.
06:37 Priya Desai: For RPO near-zero, what's the write cadence to object storage? Every token? We need to understand perf impact.
06:44 Ravi Patel: It's configurable: synchronous checkpointing after important state transitions, or asynchronous snapshotting at sub-second intervals. Usually teams pick a hybrid: critical transaction checkpoints synchronous, lower-value ephemeral caches async. We'll provide benchmark data.
06:58 Liam Chen: Competitors — we looked at BigCloudAI and ModelServeX; curious how you handle escalation differently.
07:05 Maya Ortiz: We emphasize a tight runbook and 24/7 enterprise escalation with named on-call plus a playbook repository that's customer-specific. We'll share a sample escalation matrix.
07:15 Jon Keller: Ok let's recap next steps.
07:18 Maya Ortiz: Recap: 1) Share SOC2 Type II under NDA, pen test summaries, KMS integration doc. 2) Send incident runbook and tabletop script. 3) Draft SLA addendum with 99.95 option for payments endpoints. 4) Schedule a DR tabletop in early December and a production failover rehearsal in Q1. 5) Provide RBAC/SAML/SCIM integration docs and audit log export configs.
07:39 Aisha Rahman: Good. Also include contact numbers for the on-call list.
07:42 Maya Ortiz: Will do. Anything else?
07:44 Jon Keller: No, that's it. Thanks.
07:46 Maya Ortiz: Thank you all — we'll follow up in an email with the artifacts and proposed dates. Appreciate your time.
